notes.subject: street
notes.text: Concrete roads are extremely common.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Drives on the right.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White plates with black text; older plates from the 2002 series have a green tint.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Octagonal metal poles are quite common.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: A single insulator atop a vertical bar attached to the side of a utility pole.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Centre lines can be yellow or white, and combined yellow-and-white centre lines are distinctive; yellow often looks orange.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Tall square yellow road stones, unique here.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are red on white.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Sign posts are often painted red, orange or yellow.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Tuk-tuk style tricycles are everywhere, often outnumbering cars.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs often use Latin-script text from a widely spoken world language, unlike other Southeast Asian countries; the local language also uses Latin letters.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A white car with a clearly visible black roof, or a silvery grey car also found in Bhutan.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Grain is often spread on roads to dry.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Black or white boxes on poles show a three-letter municipality code.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Motorcycle plates are colour-coded by region, with the colour strip on top in the north and at the bottom in the south.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Landlines start with 0 plus an area code; mobile numbers start 09.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A dry-sided forested mountain range with many pines in northern Luzon.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Oil palm, pineapple and banana plantations are mostly on Mindanao; sugarcane on Negros and Panay.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Diamond-pattern woven bamboo (amakan) walls are almost only in the southern half; diagonal weave is in Palawan and the north.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Yellow and black striped concrete guardrails.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: White guardrails with three recurring black stripes, unique to this southern Luzon region.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Ladder-like pole tops of two L-shaped bars joined by thin wires are unique to the capital area.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Square metal mesh poles are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A region of western Mindanao is majority Muslim, unlike the largely Christian rest.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Neon-green soft-drink bottle decorations are common in the north, especially northern Luzon.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Round grassy hills with dark brown soil beneath in central Bohol.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Near-perfect smooth cone volcano, often cloud-covered, in the south of Luzon.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A very wide, six-lane, nearly empty highway south of the main city on the long western island, with a double electrical wire.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Yellow lampposts with black stripes at the bottom.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Statues and images of ancient Roman soldiers.
